newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan seeks $1.2 billion Paris Club debt rescheduling.
newsitem.headline: Jordan seeks $1.2 billion Paris Club debt rescheduling.

text.p: Jordan hopes to conclude a deal this week with the Paris Club of official creditors to reschedule around $1.2 billion of its $6.5 billion foreign debt to push ahead economic reforms, officials said Sunday.

They said the talks with the Paris Club due to start next Thursday were the fourth such rescheduling rounds since a 1989 economic crisis when the International Monetary Fund intervened after the kingdom failed to service $8 billion of foreign debt.

The deal would reschedule interest payments due between June and early 1999. It should help Jordan reduce its debt repayment burden, currently around $500 million annually, to ensure its IMF-directed economic reforms proceed speedily.

The last major accord in June 1994 rescheduled a similar $1.2 billion of the kingdom's debts over 20 years, including 10 years' grace period. A more limited one last October rescheduled debt worth a total of $308 million slated for repayment between July 1996 and May 1997.
According to official figures, Jordan's total debt stood at $6.5 billion at the end of 1996, nearly half of which was bilateral debt to sovereign creditors.

Jordan hopes its record so far in pursuing an IMF-directed economic restructuring programme will provide it with a sympathetic hearing from official creditors who have expressed confidence in its pace and scope of free-market reforms.
